argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean certification for all named contexts. Aggregate readiness and general operational checks support certification for launch readiness, but the same record also shows that post-visit instruction summarization is a named deployment context with missing evaluation coverage. The supportable defense is therefore conditional certification only if the certification basis is explicitly limited by disclosure that this context remains an unknown-risk area rather than a passed one. The audited claim should be read as a caveated certification position, not as proof that the current packet already contains completed disclosure or risk acceptance.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost evidence is being added. On the present record, the governance objective can be met without escalation to a clean-certification dispute if the auditor treats the issue as one of certification framing: launch-readiness support exists, while the named-context gap requires a caveat rather than a block on the aggregate-readiness conclusion.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against any clean-certification reading. The admissible evidence shows the rule: material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The actor’s position is supportable only as a policy-aligned interpretation that certification must be paired with explicit disclosure of the gap. It is not supportable as a claim that the named context is already validated, nor as a claim that absence of failed tests eliminates the limitation.
concessions: The current packet does not contain admissible evidence that the final model card or certification artifact already includes the required disclosure.
The draft model-card statement treating missing evals as if they implied no known limitation is not supportable on this record.
The record does not support any clean-pass claim for post-visit instruction summarization.
